title: Unique identifier linking in user data store
description: The MongoDB users collection stores parent account data containing unique identifiers (user IDs, account IDs) that can link data to specific individuals across the system.

title: Quasi-identifier combination in user data
description: Parent account data may contain combinations of attributes (email, username, etc.) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, enabling linking of data to individuals through attribute combination.

title: Processing of identified parent account data
description: The system requests and processes identified data (parent account information) which directly identifies data subjects.

title: Unique identifier in user account data
description: The MongoDB users collection contains unique references to the identity of data subjects through user account identifiers.

title: Quasi-identifier in parent account data
description: Parent account data may contain combinations of attributes that are unique to a data subject, enabling identification through quasi-identifiers.

title: Attributable data evidence from stored accounts
description: Stored parent account data can be used to prevent an individual from denying certain claims about their account or actions.

title: Potentially sensitive parent account data types
description: Parent account data may be perceived as highly sensitive and should only be collected and processed when strictly required by the authentication service functionality.

title: Data retention beyond functional need
description: Parent account data may be stored in the MongoDB collection longer than functionally needed for the authentication service's operational requirements.

title: Excessive party access to parent account data
description: Parent account data may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, including system administrators, backup services, or other internal services.

title: Unawareness of parent account data storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their parent account information is being collected, stored, and processed by the authentication service.

title: Lack of user control over parent account data processing
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their parent account data is processed, stored, or retained.

title: Limited rectification and erasure control
description: Data subjects may lack control in rectifying incorrect parent account data or removing personal data that is no longer relevant.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More personal data may be processed than is actually needed for the authentication service's functional goals, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Parent account data may be stored longer than needed, potentially violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: Support for different data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure) may be lacking for the parent account data stored in the MongoDB collection.

title: Linking through JWT unique identifier
description: JWT tokens contain unique identifiers that can link data across systems and sessions, potentially enabling tracking of user activities.
assumptions: JWT tokens are transmitted in clear or can be intercepted

title: Identified information in JWT
description: JWT tokens contain user identity information that can be used to identify the data subject directly.
assumptions: JWT payload includes user identification data

title: Quasi-identifiers in user data
description: User data transmitted alongside JWT may contain combinations of attributes that can uniquely identify individuals.
assumptions: User data includes multiple attributes that together form quasi-identifiers

title: Data propagation to parent user
description: Personal data is propagated to the parent user service where it may not be strictly necessary for the functional goal.
assumptions: Parent user service may not need all user data transmitted

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their user data is being transmitted to the parent user service.
assumptions: Users may not have visibility into all data flows

title: Data minimization principle violation
description: More personal data is processed and transmitted than is actually needed for the authentication service functionality.
assumptions: User data includes fields not required for parent user interaction

title: Linking through parent email identifier
description: Parent email serves as a unique identifier that can link the child's login activity to the parent's identity, potentially exposing the child's usage patterns to the parent or third parties.
assumptions: Email addresses are typically unique identifiers

title: Quasi-identifier combination through email and password
description: The combination of parent email and password can serve as quasi-identifiers that may allow linking of login sessions to specific individuals.
assumptions: Email+password combination may be unique enough for identification

title: Processing of identified data during child login
description: The authentication service processes identified personal data (parent email and password) during the child login process, which directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: Email and password are clearly identifiable personal data

title: Email as unique identifier for data subject
description: Parent email contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (parent), which is processed during child authentication.

title: Collection of highly sensitive password data
description: Password is a highly sensitive data type that should only be collected when strictly required. The system collects and processes passwords during authentication.

title: Unnecessary processing of password data
description: Password data is processed for authentication purposes, but the extent of processing (storage, logging, etc.) may exceed what is functionally needed for the login functionality.
assumptions: Password processing may include unnecessary storage or analysis

title: Child unawareness of data processing implications
description: The child user may not be fully aware of the implications of using parent credentials for authentication, including data collection and processing.
assumptions: Children may lack understanding of privacy implications

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: The child user has limited control over how their authentication data is processed, stored, or shared with the authentication service.
assumptions: Children typically have limited privacy controls

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Collecting parent email and password for child login may process more personal data than functionally necessary, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle may be violated

title: Potential invalid consent for child data processing
description: Children may not provide valid consent for processing their authentication data, especially when using parent credentials, raising consent validity concerns.
assumptions: Child consent may be legally insufficient

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The video upload flow processes identified personal data (videos containing identifiable content of the parent user and potentially other individuals).

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content inherently contains revealing attributes (faces, activities, environment) that support identification of the data subject and potentially others.

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is strictly functionally required for video upload and approval/rejection.

title: Unnecessary video processing and analysis
description: Video data may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched (e.g., for quality control, metadata extraction) beyond what is necessary for the approval/rejection functionality.

title: Unawareness of video data processing
description: The parent user may not be fully aware of the extent of video data collection, processing, storage, or disclosure that occurs during the upload and approval workflow.

title: Lack of user control over video processing preferences
description: The parent user may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their video data is processed, stored, or shared.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data processing may exceed what is actually needed for the functional goal of upload and approval/rejection, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.

title: Excessive party exposure to video data
description: Video data may be made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary (e.g., administrators, auditors, third-party services) during the approval/rejection process.

title: Excessive video data retention
description: Video data may be stored longer than functionally needed for the approval/rejection workflow, creating unnecessary privacy risk.

title: Sensitive video data type collected
description: Video data is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected and processed beyond what is functionally required for streaming approved content to a child user.

title: Excessive video granularity
description: Video streaming may provide fine-grained visual data about the child that is more detailed than necessary for the intended functionality of streaming approved content.

title: Unnecessary video processing
description: Video data may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched beyond what is needed to achieve the functional goal of streaming approved video to the child.

title: Data shared with predetermined parties
description: Video data is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties (the child user) which may be more than functionally necessary.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system processes identified data (video content) that can be associated with the child user as the data subject.

title: Revealing attributes in video
description: Video content may include revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject (child user) through visual or contextual information.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in video
description: Video data may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., location, time, context) that can be combined to link data to the individual child user.

title: Profiling through video analysis
description: Video data of the child can be analyzed for patterns to link data to that individual, potentially revealing behavioral patterns or preferences.

title: Unawareness of video processing
description: The child user (data subject) may not be fully aware about the collection, processing, or storage of their video data during streaming.

title: Lack of control over video preferences
description: The child user may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their video data is processed, collected, or stored.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Video data processing may exceed what is actually needed, violating the data minimization principle under GDPR.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in browsing data
description: Browsing data sent to advertisers may contain unique identifiers (e.g., device IDs, cookies, IP addresses) that can be used to link data to specific individuals across different contexts.

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Browsing data contains multiple attributes (page views, timestamps, device info) that can be combined to create quasi-identifiers, enabling re-identification of individuals.

title: Profiling an individual through browsing patterns
description: Advertisers can analyze browsing data to build profiles of individuals, inferring interests, behaviors, and potentially sensitive attributes through pattern analysis.

title: Processing of identifiable information
description: Browsing data may contain unique references to the identity of data subjects (e.g., user IDs, session tokens) that are processed and shared with third-party advertisers.

title: Revealing attributes in browsing data
description: Browsing data includes revealing attributes such as visited pages, search queries, and interaction patterns that support identification of data subjects and their interests.

title: Data propagation to third-party advertisers
description: Browsing data is propagated to third-party advertisers where it may be used beyond the original functional purpose of the AI recommendation engine.

title: Data shared with predetermined set of parties
description: Browsing data is shared with a predetermined set of third-party advertisers, expanding exposure beyond what may be functionally necessary for the recommendation engine.

title: Unawareness of data processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their browsing data is being collected, processed, and shared with third-party advertisers for advertising purposes.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Browsing data may be processed and shared with advertisers beyond what is actually needed for the functional goals of the AI recommendation engine.

title: Potential invalid consent for data sharing
description: Consent for sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may not be valid, informed, or freely given, potentially violating GDPR requirements.

title: Processing of identified data - Government ID images
description: The Authentication Service processes government ID images which are clearly identified personal data that directly identifies individuals.

title: Identifier in government ID images
description: Government ID images contain unique identifiers (government ID numbers, biometric data) that directly reference the identity of the data subject.

title: Revealing attributes in ID images
description: Government ID images reveal multiple identifying attributes including facial features, name, ID number, and other personal information that supports identification of the data subject.

title: Highly sensitive data type stored
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required. Storing them in a file system may exceed functional necessity.

title: Data retention concerns
description: Unclear how long government ID images are retained in the file system. Storage may exceed functionally needed duration, violating storage limitation principles.

title: Excessive party access to ID images
description: File system storage may grant access to more parties than functionally necessary, including system administrators, backup services, or other internal services that may not need access to government ID images.

title: Unawareness of ID image storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their government ID images are being stored in the file system, particularly if this is part of an authentication process they don't fully understand.

title: Lack of user control over ID image processing
description: Data subjects likely have no control over preferences, consent, or customization regarding how their government ID images are processed and stored.

title: Lack of rectification/erasure control
description: Data subjects may lack the ability to request rectification of incorrect ID image data or erasure of their government ID images from the file system.

title: GDPR data minimization violation
description: Storing government ID images may process more personal data than actually needed for authentication functionality, violating the data minimization principle under GDPR.

title: GDPR storage limitation violation
description: Unclear retention policies for government ID images may result in storing data longer than functionally needed, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.

title: Potential invalid consent for ID image collection
description: If consent is used as the lawful basis for collecting government ID images, it may not be valid consent as users may not have meaningful choice or understanding of the implications.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in child history
description: Child history data likely contains unique identifiers (e.g., child ID, birth date, medical record numbers) that can be used to link data across systems or contexts.
assumptions: Child history contains identifiable or quasi-identifiable information

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: Combination of attributes in child history (e.g., age, location, medical conditions) can serve as quasi-identifiers that may uniquely identify the child when combined.
assumptions: Child history contains multiple attributes that can be combined for identification

title: Processing of identified child data
description: The system processes child history which is identified personal data about the child, not just the parent.
assumptions: Child history contains personal data that identifies the child
